title: Battle City
romNote: Namco 1985 (J), NROM 24592 bytes. The RAM map below was measured with jsnes (data/bc-explore), not copied from a wiki.
playersNote: The human is player 1 (yellow tank, spawns left of the base), the AI player 2 (green tank, spawns right). Only controller 1 works on the title screen and the stage curtain, so the AI's SELECT/START taps go to controller 1 (start.controller) while it plays on controller 2. Both tanks are otherwise identical.

ram.note: gameRoutine $50: 2 = title screen, 0 otherwise. levelRoutine $6a: ff at boot/title, 3 = stage curtain / score screen, 0-2 = playing (it cycles through the three enemy spawn points). playerMode $83 is the title cursor: 0 = 1 player, 1 = 2 players, 2 = construction. lives $51/$52 are ff on the title. level $85 = stage number (ff on the title). invincible $89/$8a = spawn-shield seconds left.

start.note: Title: SELECT moves the cursor (playerMode 0/1/2), START begins; then a 'STAGE n' curtain waits for START again (A/B there change the stage, so never press them). After a game over the game returns to the title on its own.

tank.note: Object table of 8 tanks: slots 0/1 are the players, 2-7 enemies. x/y are the tank centre (16x16 body, snapped to an 8 px lattice, playfield centres 24..216). sprite: a0-a3 = moving up/left/down/right (low 2 bits = direction), 84-8b = standing (direction not encoded), e0-fd = spawning sparkle (invulnerable), 11-73 = exploding, 00 = not present (x is then ff). flags: 80 = enemy, 40 = frozen by the clock item.
tank.bulletsNote: 10 bullet slots, slot i = bullet of tank i (8/9 = the players' second bullets after a star). state: 4d = flying in direction d (0 up, 1 left, 2 down, 3 right), 3x/2x/1x = impact animation, 00 = free. Bullets fly 2 px/frame (4 for power tanks / upgraded players); two bullets that meet destroy each other; a player bullet that hits the partner only stuns them.
tank.itemNote: Power-up on the field: x centre (0 = none), y centre, type (0 helmet, 1 clock, 2 shovel, 3 star, 4 grenade, 5 tank).
tank.mapNote: Shadow of the PPU name table: 32 bytes per 8 px row, 30 rows, tile ids. Cell (cx, cy) = $0400 + cy*32 + cx covers screen x cx*8..+8, y cy*8..+8. Playfield cells 2..27 on both axes. A bullet is 8 px wide and centred on the lattice, so it straddles two cells; a brick cell takes two hits (0f -> partial -> 00).

coachBrief: Battle City (NES, 1985, Namco) is a top-down tank game on a 13x13-tile arena. Each stage sends 20 enemy tanks from the three spawn points along the top edge; they are all destroyed to clear the stage. The players' base is the eagle at the bottom centre, walled with bricks: if an enemy shell hits the eagle the game is over for both players, whatever their lives. Tanks move up/down/left/right, one shell in flight at a time (two after a star). Shells destroy brick walls (two hits per brick cell), bounce off steel, pass over water and trees. Two shells that meet destroy each other, so a tank can shoot down an incoming shell. Enemy types: basic (slow), fast, power (fast shells), armour (takes four hits). Every fourth, eleventh and eighteenth enemy flashes red: killing it drops a power-up: helmet (shield), clock (freezes enemies), shovel (steel walls around the eagle for a while), star (upgrades the tank: faster shells, then two shells, then shells that break steel), grenade (destroys every enemy on screen), tank (extra life). A player's own shell only stuns the partner, but do not do it. Priorities for the buddy: stay alive (dodge or shoot down incoming shells), protect the eagle, then destroy enemies; do not shoot toward the eagle or its brick wall; collect power-ups when it is safe. The human is player 1 (yellow tank, left of the base); the buddy is player 2 (green tank, right of the base).
